# nanoflags_flag_environment (Resource)

A flag's configuration in one environment: on/off, the default and off values, and targeting rules (fixed values or percentage rollouts).

This edits the environment's **draft**, exactly like the dashboard. Nothing reaches SDKs until the draft is published, with `nanoflags_environment_publish` or through the dashboard's review flow in environments that require approvals. The resource owns the whole rule list: rules not declared here are removed from the draft. Destroying the resource leaves the draft as it is (the API has no way to remove a flag from one environment).

Scopes: `flags:read`, `flags:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nanoflags_flag_environment" "new_checkout_production" {
  project       = "web"
  flag          = nanoflags_flag.new_checkout.key
  environment   = "production"
  enabled       = true
  default_value = jsonencode(false)
  off_value     = jsonencode(false)

  # Internal users always get the new checkout.
  rule {
    id          = "staff"
    description = "Company accounts"
    condition {
      attribute = "email"
      op        = "ends_with"
      value     = jsonencode("@example.com")
    }
    value = jsonencode(true)
  }

  # 25% of Pro customers, bucketed per account.
  rule {
    id = "pro-rollout"
    condition {
      op    = "segment"
      value = jsonencode(nanoflags_segment.pro_customers.key)
    }
    rollout {
      percentage = 25
      value      = jsonencode(true)
      otherwise  = jsonencode(false)
      bucket_by  = "accountId"
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `environment` (String) Environment key or id, e.g. `production`.
- `flag` (String) Flag key.
- `project` (String) Project key or id.

### Optional

- `default_value` (String) JSON-encoded value served when the flag is on and no rule matches, e.g. `jsonencode(true)`. Kept as it is when omitted.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the flag is on. When off, every evaluation gets `off_value`. Kept as it is when omitted.
- `off_value` (String) JSON-encoded value served while the flag is off. Kept as it is when omitted.
- `rule` (Block List) Targeting rule, evaluated in order; the first match serves. Set exactly one of `value` (a fixed value) or a `rollout` block. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<project>/<flag>/<environment>`.

<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `id` (String) Stable rule id, unique within the flag, e.g. `beta-users`. Evaluation reasons and insights refer to it.

Optional:

- `condition` (Block List) A targeting condition. All or any conditions must hold, depending on `match`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule--condition))
- `description` (String) What the rule is for.
- `match` (String) `all` (default): every condition must hold; `any`: one is enough. A rule without conditions matches everyone.
- `rollout` (Block, Optional) Percentage rollout: matching contexts inside the allocation get `value`, the others `otherwise`. Bucketing is deterministic. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule--rollout))
- `value` (String) JSON-encoded fixed value served to matching contexts.

<a id="nestedblock--rule--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.condition`

Required:

- `op` (String) Operator: `eq`, `neq`, `in`, `not_in`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte` (numbers), `semver_eq`, `semver_neq`, `semver_gt`, `semver_gte`, `semver_lt`, `semver_lte` (semantic versions such as `4.10.0`), `before`, `after` (dates: `2026-12-31`, `2026-12-31T09:00:00Z` or a Unix timestamp), `exists`, `not_exists`, `segment`, `not_segment`. SDK releases from before the version and date operators evaluate those conditions as not matching.

Optional:

- `attribute` (String) Context attribute, e.g. `plan` or `key`. Ignored (leave empty) for the `segment` and `not_segment` operators.
- `value` (String) JSON-encoded comparison value, e.g. `jsonencode(["pro", "team"])` for `in`, or `jsonencode("beta-users")` (a segment key) for `segment`. Omit for `exists` / `not_exists`.


<a id="nestedblock--rule--rollout"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.rollout`

Optional:

- `bucket_by` (String) Context attribute used for bucketing. Default: `key`.
- `otherwise` (String) JSON-encoded value for matching contexts outside the allocation.
- `percentage` (Number) 0–100, up to two decimals.
- `seed` (String) Bucketing seed. Default: the flag key, so allocations are independent per flag.
- `value` (String) JSON-encoded value inside the allocation.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project key>/<flag key>/<environment key>
terraform import nanoflags_flag_environment.new_checkout_production web/new-checkout/production
```
